device.name: LeRobot SO-101 teleoperation in Isaac Lab: Rock-A-Stack Simple

facts.text: Lerobot-So101-Teleop-Rock-A-Stack-Simple is registered with gymnasium, with entry point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv and env_cfg_entry_point rock_a_stack_env_cfg:RockAStackSimpleEnvCfg
RockAStackSimpleEnvCfg extends BaseEnvCfg
BaseEnvCfg extends Isaac Lab's ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg
The action term is a JointPositionActionCfg over the six joints Rotation, Pitch, Elbow, Wrist_Pitch, Wrist_Roll and Jaw, with scale 1 and use_default_offset False
The policy observation group has one term, joint_pos, with corruption disabled
The visual observation group has camera_ego and camera_external RGB terms, with corruption disabled and concatenate_terms False
camera_ego is a 480 x 640 RGB camera
camera_external is a 480 x 640 RGB camera
The environment uses decimation 2 and a simulation timestep of 1/120 s, so one policy step is 1/60 s
The configured episode length is 5 s
The base environment declares rewards and terminations as None for teleoperation
The scene is configured with one environment (num_envs = 1)
The Rock-A-Stack Simple scene adds a rock-a-stack asset, a base plate and five rings named Ring01 to Ring05

The reset event randomizes the base plate pose with the ranges written as x (0.15 - 0.2, 0.3 - 0.2), y (0.0, -0.15), z (0.04, 0.04) and yaw (-0.5, 0.5), and the five rings' offsets as x (-0.1, 0.1) and y (0.25, 0.1)
The task creates a physics material with static friction 0.5, dynamic friction 0.5 and restitution 0.5
The SO-101 robot asset spawns the USD file usd/SO-ARM101-USD.usd
The SO-101 asset's initial joint positions are Rotation -0.2736, Pitch -0.6109, Elbow -0.0745, Wrist_Pitch 1.5148, Wrist_Roll -1.6034 and Jaw -0.1465
The agent script creates the environment with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg)
The agent script passes obs['policy'][0] and obs['visual'] to the dataset processor
The teleop agent drives the simulation from a real leader arm on /dev/ttyACM0 with kind leader
The README badges pin Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and Isaac Lab 2.3.0
The README installs Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and Isaac Lab v2.3.0 before this repository
The README installs this repository with uv pip install -e source/lerobot_so101_teleop
The README describes a sample environment for the LeRobot SO-101 robot in Isaac Lab to collect demonstrations in simulation
The README's run example is lerobot_agent --task Lerobot-So101-Teleop-Rock-A-Stack-Simple
The package requires Python 3.11 or newer

determinism.notes: the fake reseeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1, but its observation is a constant zero frame and the held joint positions do not depend on the seed, so a seed changes no observable value; the upstream seed controls Isaac Lab's generators and the Rock-A-Stack reset draws, and the two were not compared because the upstream stack was not run

gaps: kinematic F0 stand-in: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuator, sensor, noise, renderer or domain randomisation; a step holds the commanded six joint positions and returns them, and the reward is a constant 0.0 (the clone declares rewards None, base_env_cfg.py:290)

the real action space is the Box of Isaac Lab's action manager for the joint-position term; the clone states the six joints and the scale (base_env_cfg.py:141-146) but no numeric bound, so the fake publishes an unbounded six-element Box and the bridge has no action envelope to probe

the real observation is a Dict of the policy group (the robot's joint positions) and the visual group (camera_ego and camera_external at 480 x 640 x 3 RGB each, base_env_cfg.py:75-80, :105-110, :163-186); the fake returns the same group names but 18 flat values per camera instead of a 480 x 640 x 3 image

the upstream environment is vectorised over num_envs and returns batched tensors; the scene is configured with one environment (base_env_cfg.py:300) and the fake serves one environment with Python lists

the Rock-A-Stack reset randomises the base plate, five rings, physics material and lighting (rock_a_stack_env_cfg.py:66-115); the fake's reset only reseeds its RNG and holds zero joint positions, so no randomised scene is modelled

truncation: the fake ends an episode after 300 steps, derived from episode_length_s 5 s at the 1/60 s policy step (base_env_cfg.py:297-298, :305); the upstream truncation is implemented in Isaac Lab outside the clone and was not observed

the sim path gymnasium.make('Lerobot-So101-Teleop-Rock-A-Stack-Simple') was not run: it needs Isaac Sim 5.1.0, Isaac Lab v2.3.0, Python 3.11 and a GPU (README.md:4-5, :38-47), and the driver cannot pass a parsed cfg because building it imports the clone's modules
the fake was never compared with an Isaac Sim run; Python lists are used instead of torch tensors and the cameras are constant placeholders

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the runtime latches the e-stop: no further step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, the simulation does not advance, and the last observation stays readable
